/floor-games:
Floor games

One sticker. Four ways to play.

Pick a game by what your child enjoys: hopping, making music, telling stories or solving a puzzle together.

Peach Pop

One foot on 1. Two feet on 2 and 3. Follow the numbers to 10, then make up a challenge for the way back.

Wiggleway

Turn a coloured ribbon into a tune: clap on yellow, then add a second beat on blue. Next time, turn the same trail into a story.

Jump Jamboree

Feet together, feet apart. Follow six rows of stepping pads, then turn the dots into a clapping tune.

Fork & Friends

Start at opposite blue rings. Can you swap places without sharing a spot? Take turns and give each other room.
/play/hopscotch-peach-pop:
Floor games

Peach Pop

Pick one way to play. Learn the rule, then put the phone away.

1. Hop to Ten

1 child

Start just below 1. Step onto 1, then place one foot on each square of the next pair. Follow the numbers to 10. Walk back beside the sticker. Try small hops when comfortable.

2. Secret Stop

1 or more

Choose a number before you start. Travel in order and freeze when you reach it; on a pair, freeze when either number is your choice. Finish at 10. Next round, choose two stops.

3. Echo Squares

2 or more, taking turns

The leader walks from 1 to 10 and waves on one chosen row. The next child repeats the wave in the same place and adds a clap on another row. Keep building until you want a fresh sequence.

4. Ten-Tale Trail

1 or more

Choose a character and a place. At each row add a sentence to their adventure. Give the story an ending at 10. On the next trip a new storyteller can choose a new character.

Use a clear, level indoor floor. Start by walking; try jumps only when comfortable. Take turns unless a game calls for two players on separate spots.

/play/wiggleway:
Floor games

Wiggleway

Pick one way to play. Learn the rule, then put the phone away.

1. Colour Composer

1 child

Choose an endpoint and a colour. Walk the ribbon to the other end. Clap once on your chosen colour and stay quiet on the others. Next round give a second colour two claps. Finish a whole trail without mixing up your tune.

2. Growing Journey

1 child

Begin on a ring. Visit the next spot and return home. Then visit the next two spots and return. Add one spot each trip. Say the colours on the outward journey; on the return, try to say each next colour before looking down. Reach the far ring to finish.

3. Echo Parade

2 or more, taking turns

The leader walks the whole trail, adding a clap, wave or freeze at ONE chosen spot. The next player repeats the journey and adds one action at a new spot. Keep the same order. When someone forgets, help them and begin a fresh parade.

4. Story Steps

1 or more, taking turns

Choose what each colour means: a place, a creature, an object or a surprise. Travel the trail and add one spoken sentence at each stop using that colour’s meaning. Reach the final ring to finish the story. Next trip, change the meanings.

Use a clear, level indoor floor. Start by walking; try jumps only when comfortable. Take turns unless a game calls for two players on separate spots.

/play/jump-jamboree:
Floor games

Jump Jamboree

Pick one way to play. Learn the rule, then put the phone away.

1. Together / Apart

1 child

Start at the bottom single pad. Move one row forward at a time: land with feet together on a single pad and one foot on each pad of a pair. Pause to balance after each landing. Finish at the top. Practise by stepping before trying jumps.

2. Dot Orchestra

1 child

Walk up the track. At each row, clap the number of dots on ONE pad: one or two. Keep your feet still while clapping. After reaching the top, turn around and play the rhythm backwards. Can you do both directions without a missed beat?

3. Copy My Six

2 or more, taking turns

The composer walks the six rows and chooses one action per row: clap, wave or freeze. Everyone watches. The next child follows and copies all six in order. Begin with only two rows; extend the sequence when the group is ready. Swap composer each round.

4. Silent Landing

1 child or a cooperative group

Make one trip, stepping or making small two-foot jumps to the next row. Pause at each arrival and judge your landing: quiet and steady, or try again. Count how many of the six rows felt controlled. Repeat to match your best; the goal is control, not speed or distance.

Use a clear, level indoor floor. Start by walking; try jumps only when comfortable. Take turns unless a game calls for two players on separate spots.

/play/fork-and-friends:
Floor games

Fork & Friends

Pick one way to play. Learn the rule, then put the phone away.

1. Find Another Way

1 child

Walk from one blue ring to the other along the printed links. Do not revisit a spot on that trip. Return around the outside of the sticker, then find a different route. Begin with two different routes. There are six shortest routes to discover.

2. Yellow Detour

1 child

Travel from ring to ring without touching yellow. Try both sides. Next, make a trip that MUST visit yellow. Finally visit both outermost spots in one trip without revisiting a spot. Walk the connections; this is a thinking challenge.

3. Meet in the Middle?

2 children

Start on opposite blue rings. Take turns moving along ONE link to an empty spot. Work together to exchange starting places. Never share a spot or pass through each other. Use the side branches to make room. After succeeding, try with fewer total moves.

4. Route Director

2 children

One child stands on a blue ring; the other is the director. Before the walker moves, the director says the colours for an entire route to the opposite ring. The walker follows one link at a time. If a colour offers two choices, the director must also point. Swap roles after each trip.

Use a clear, level indoor floor. Start by walking; try jumps only when comfortable. Take turns unless a game calls for two players on separate spots.
